## Purpose

One blood collection produces two distinct analytical materials. **Plasma** supplies cell-free DNA for EM-seq and fragmentomics; **serum** supplies sIgA for ELISA. Tube type, clotting, centrifugation, transfer, delay, temperature, freeze–thaw history, aliquot volume, and visible hemolysis belong in the data record.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  B[Blood collection] --> P[Plasma aliquots]
  B --> S[Serum aliquots]
  P --> C[cfDNA extraction]
  S --> E[sIgA ELISA]
```

| Fraction | Immediate output | Later data |
|---|---|---|
| plasma | labeled, frozen aliquots with processing metadata | cfDNA yield, methylation counts, plasma fragment features |
| serum | labeled, frozen aliquots with processing metadata | replicate OD and calibrated sIgA concentration |

## QC gate

Processing must prevent cellular carryover into plasma: leukocyte lysis can swamp rare colon-derived cfDNA and distort fragment sizes. Serum conditions must be consistent enough that plate differences are not proxies for clinical group.

::: {.callout-important title="Plasma is not serum"}
The fractions are not interchangeable. Plasma cfDNA is sequenced; serum sIgA is measured optically. They meet only after independent QC.
:::
